evals.prompt: Run a Delphi study with a panel of experts on the year fault-tolerant quantum computing reaches commercial advantage — rounds, median, IQR, and the dissenting view.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Scopes the question to a single scalar with an explicit event definition; Elicits round 1 independently, then feeds back the median and IQR anonymously; Stops on stability rather than unanimity and states the stopping reason; Reports the median with the Q1-Q3 band and preserves the dissenting rationale.
expectations: Scopes the question to a single scalar with an explicit event definition
Elicits round 1 independently, then feeds back the median and IQR anonymously
Stops on stability rather than unanimity and states the stopping reason
Reports the median with the Q1-Q3 band and preserves the dissenting rationale

evals.prompt: Five senior engineers each give a different date for when our robotaxi service breaks even, and the loudest voice wins every meeting. Is there a structured way to get an anonymous group estimate with the spread of expert opinion?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Diagnoses deference bias and prescribes anonymous, independent elicitation; Runs iterated rounds with controlled feedback of the group distribution; Reports the spread rather than only a single number.
expectations: Diagnoses deference bias and prescribes anonymous, independent elicitation
Runs iterated rounds with controlled feedback of the group distribution
Reports the spread rather than only a single number

evals.prompt: We need a consensus forecast from external experts on when EU regulators will approve this therapy class, and we can't get them in a room. What method gives us a defensible aggregated estimate with the spread of opinion?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Defines panel size and heterogeneity, including at least one skeptic; Never weights answers by self-rated expertise; Distinguishes consensus from a persistent split and refuses to average a bimodal panel.
expectations: Defines panel size and heterogeneity, including at least one skeptic
Never weights answers by self-rated expertise
Distinguishes consensus from a persistent split and refuses to average a bimodal panel

evals.prompt: Aggregate these round-two panel estimates: compute the median, interquartile range, and tell me whether the panel has stabilised or needs another round.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Computes median, Q1, Q3 and flags estimates outside the IQR with their rationales; Applies the 15% stability level to decide STABLE versus MOVING; Uses the companion script scripts/delphi.py rather than mental arithmetic.
expectations: Computes median, Q1, Q3 and flags estimates outside the IQR with their rationales
Applies the 15% stability level to decide STABLE versus MOVING
Uses the companion script scripts/delphi.py rather than mental arithmetic

evals.prompt: When will on-device inference overtake cloud APIs for enterprise summarization? Give me a dated prediction with accelerants, blockers and kill-signals.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Produces one dated prediction with a confidence and kill-signals; Does not convene or simulate an expert panel.
expectations: Produces one dated prediction with a confidence and kill-signals
Does not convene or simulate an expert panel

evals.prompt: My last 30 forecasts have resolved — compute my Brier score and tell me if I was overconfident.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Scores resolved forecasts and decomposes calibration versus resolution; Does not run elicitation rounds.
expectations: Scores resolved forecasts and decomposes calibration versus resolution
